Journal/2026/2026-06-June/2026-06-06-sme.content:
I woke at 03:00 with a hip that felt a little wrong, nor hurting exactly, but like something sat a little wrong. So I got up and turned on the DownDog app on a yoga + pilates session and did 30 minutes, often substituting hip exercises for other stuff. Then I went back to sleep till sometime after 07:00, which gave me time for breakfast and gathering food to take with us to the demo.
The demo was at the smithy, and I tried making another belt hook. It is impressive how much I have forgotten since October when last I did any smithing. I managed, eventually, with some help from Keldor, but I didn’t try another because he really cranked up the heat so he could do some forge welding, which seemed to go well. He left it in the cooling forge to normalise.
After the demo we went home, I repacked food into my backpack,  put away the nettles that I dried overnight, and relaxed a little before we had to head to head to thr train station in Umeå.
The train left at 21:30, and should arrive in Stockholm just after 06:00.

Journal/2026/2026-06-June/2026-06-07-a-t.content:
Morning train trips
I woke about a half an hour before we arrived in Stockholm, which gave me time to buy a ticket to Linköping, pack my pillows back into my backpack and generally get ready to go. Alas, the fast train with no changes departed about 10 minutes before we were due to arrive in Stockholm. The next option, an hour after we arrive, requires changing trains in Katrineholm, but was cheaper than the no-changes fast tran heaper than the no-changes fast train that departs another hour later, so I booked it.
That gave me time to do a 30 minutes standing stretches yoga session at the station before heading to the platform. I thought about working on the train, but I started with updating this, and then there was only 40 minutes remaining before we should arrive, so I don’t know if I will accomplish anything. I should, as tomorrow is a work day, and I suspect I will still be travelling…
I did manage to empty my work in box during that time, changed trains, then had enough time in Linköping to do some yoga with pilates before catching the train to Motala, where Rebeccah and Petter picked me up.
social time and adventures
We went back to their place in Vadstena, made lunch, and then went in to town to look at the new exhibition on Female authors of the Middle Ages at the Cloister Museum. Of course, one of the featured authors is Vadstena’s own St. Briggita.

Medieval Women Authors Exhibit






Some photos from Birgitta’s Cloister


 add the rest, there are lots

Road trip
After the museum I took a 10 minute nap, repacked my car a little  to improve accessibility to the bed and put snacks in reach and started driving.
Stop one was a Biltema in Motala, as we had taken the usb plugs from my car to use in Keldor’s when we abandoned mine to be fixed after Double Wars.
I had thought to visit Holmfrid in the Örebro area as my next stop, till I checked the map, and saw that they are far enough the wrong direction from Örebro that the detour would have added two full hours to the trip, not counting time to hang out. So I decided to save that adventure for another day, and instead went to Agnes apartment in Skultuna to pick up the dinosaur stencils she is getting rid of that Keldor wants, arriving at 18:47.
We hung out and chatted over tea for a bit, and I fed her some of my Dandelion cookies. Then I contibuted to her get ready to move to the house she recently bought, by washing a load of dishes, thereby freeing up that bit of energy for packing
I got back on the road about 20:00, and reached Gävle around 21:40, where I bought a couple of bottles of Vitamin Well Awake and a bag of chrunchy cheetoes to keep me awake while driving.  I added some of the Well Awake to my water bottle, and, despite not being hungry, nibbled on the Cheetoes to try to keep energy levels up.
I reached Tönnebro at 22:30, took a 1.5 hour nap, went to the loo, and went back to sleep for another 1.5 hours.

Journal/2026/2026-06-June/2026-06-08-lon.filePath: Journal/2026/2026-06 June/2026-06-08 long drive, day two.md
Journal/2026/2026-06-June/2026-06-08-lon.title: 2026-06-08 long drive, day two
Journal/2026/2026-06-June/2026-06-08-lon.content:
I slept at Tönnebro till 02:15, did some yoga, and started driving again at 02:47.
I stopped again at the 24 hour gas station just south of Sundsvall at 04:18, filled the tank, used the loo, bought a berry juice, naped for 20 minutes, and got back on the road.
Keldor woke and called me at 05:38 as he drove to work, keeping me company till 06:30, when he arrived at work, and I reached the rest area by the hotel at the Högakustenbrön, where I slept for just over an hour.
Then I drove on to Skuleberget,  napped for an hour, and then took my computer to the cafe for my 10:00 meeting, after which I took a walk a very short distance up the hill, before deciding it was nap time, so I returned to the car for another 40 minutes sleep.
I got back on the road at 12:20, stopped at the large grocery store in Örnsköldsvik to use the loo, and buy some fresh veg—after so much junk on the roadtrip, I will need some.
The next stop was the has station in Umeå, where I bought a black current and vanilla ice cream popsicle that was so good I went back in and bought a second.

Keldor called me just as I bought the first, and when I told him what I was eating he commented that it had been made for me. It really was.
I finally reached home at 16:50, unloaded only food, computer bag, and my pillows, and curled up with a book for a bit. The event stuff can wait for tomorrow.
Keldor came home from work a bit later, with his new purchace, a second hand EmcoStar all in one compact shop tool, like the one in this blog. He bought it from a retired guy who doesn’t use it any more, who had inherited it from his dad.

He paid for it yesterday and picked it up today, and when there the guy asked him, would you also like a knife sharpening machine? Yes, yes he would.
By 18:00 Keldor was feeling like a nap, and I was super tired, so we went to lay down for a bit, and woke more than two hours later. He got up and had dinner, I started adding recent photos to my blogs and replying to messages, and before I knew it, it was after midnight. oops. Road trips do weird things to one’s sleep schedule.

Journal/2026/2026-06-June/2026-06-09-not.filePath: Journal/2026/2026-06 June/2026-06-09 not recovered from the drive.md
Journal/2026/2026-06-June/2026-06-09-not.title: 2026-06-09 not recovered from the drive
Journal/2026/2026-06-June/2026-06-09-not.content:
Keldor’s alarm went off this morning at the wrong point in my sleep cycle, and I didn’t want to get up. But I didn’t want to miss our morning phone call as he drives to work, either, so I got up, and, as we chatted I put away a couple of things and dealt with the washer that I had started on an 8-hour delay before heading to bed.
After he went to work I sat at the computer and started working myself, but by 09:00 I was too sleepy to keep my eyes open, so I went back to bed, and slept for the better part of an hour.
Then I made some Spegetti squash and green sauce for  lunch and returned to work. Just as I figured out what I should be doing Keldor called. Since I can’t focus on work while chatting I moved to the couch with some frozen berry mousse for desert, and two hours later I hadn’t convinced myself to get off the couch and resume working. Like I haven’t really recovered from driving the car north (I haven’t).
Then I fell asleep on the couch for 15 minutes, till Keldor called on his way home from work. That woke me enough to go get another bowl of squash and green sauce as we talked.
Which gave me the energy to brush Kali, who had been asking for attention. (Keldor, in the mran time, got home and went out to mow the lawn.)
Then I headed to the cellar and got out the roll of wet room wall paper to measure it for the new bathroom wall in the basement.
But then I couldn’t find the folding measuring stick, and came up stairs to see if one was here. By then Keldor had finished the lawn and was relaxing on the couch,  and he said he has no idea where it was.
So I sat down next to him and read a book before updating this. The wallpaper cam wait for tomorrow.

Journal/2026/2026-06-June/2026-06-10-mus.filePath: Journal/2026/2026-06 June/2026-06-10 must be recovered,  I stayed up too late.md
Journal/2026/2026-06-June/2026-06-10-mus.title: 2026-06-10 must be recovered,  I stayed up too late
Journal/2026/2026-06-June/2026-06-10-mus.content:
Work
I went in to work today for the Swedigarch Monthly meeting, and left the meeting inspired and energised about work, so I guess this means that I not only have a fun job, but good colleagues, too.
I like our new summer intern, Bruno,  too, which is good, as I will be their contact person when everyone else is on vacation.
Inspiration to start a project I haven’t time for
Since the meeting ended at 12:00, I caught the 12:30 bus, and happily worked, ticking off many simple to-dos arising from the meeting, till we got to Sikeå, when I suddenly couldn’t keep my eyes open any longer, so I packed up the computer and took a 20 minute nap, after which we were close enough to home I didn’t bother reopening the computer, and checked notifications instead
One of them led me to a cool resource:
bardictorch.miraheze.org/wiki/Get_Started_Contributing
I have been thinking of adding a bardic section to this blog, and copying over my songs from Trello, but this really encourages me to do so, so I can link my stuff there, and make it available to others. Besides, there are no Swedish songs there, yet. (But no time to start thay today)
How’s Hugo doing?
On my walk home from the bus I went past Bryan’s to see how Hugo wwas getting on.

Good little lawn mower! Having Hugo running daily has transformed the lawn into a groomed service.
A yummy interlude
Then I went home, cooked my artichoke, and, as it cooked, made an experimental batch of Browned butter and roasted almond candy, which I carefully didn’t try until after eating my artichoke. I attemped to walk away from the candy four times. I finally succeded, but I think I ate about half the batch before I escaped to the cellar, far from temptation.
Home improvements
While Keldor finished mowing our lawn I cut the fibreglass wallpaper to cover the wall in the downstairs bathroom.
Then we played a quick game of Qwirkle as he ate dinner before we hung the paper. Now we can paint the walls tomorrow.
Unloaded the car
After we finished the wallpaper I was inspired to put away the stuff in the luggage I hadn’t yet dealt with after getting home on Monday.
Having done that, I was inspired to start unloading the car, thinking that I would put away a couple of things, and save the rest for tomorrow.
But I was having so much fun putting things where they belong, that I just kept going. I didn’t stop till the only things left in the van were the box that lives upstsirs in the entry way and Keldor’s new spit-roasting grill. We don’t yet have an “away” for the grill yet, and the chest can sit there till tomorrow, when we can drive the car around to the front of the house.
Stayed up too late
Then I went upstairs, spent quite a while in various conversations on Messenger, did my yoga, and updated this. I would wonder how it is nearly midnight already, but I think I know.
Of course, I didn’t go to sleep straight away
Instead, I started filling in some of the songs I have written on the new bardic section of my blog. In just over an hour, I only managed to copy over my first year’s Norrskensbard entries:

Prologue to the Canterbury Tales
Winter time it has arrived
Norra Nordmark
Genom merskog

But now I will sleep!

Journal/2026/2026-06-June/2026-06-11-a-k.title: 2026-06-11 a kindred spirit
Journal/2026/2026-06-June/2026-06-11-a-k.content:
This morning
Despite my late night last night, I managed to get up on time this morning and took the bus to town.
I had enough to do on the bus that I didn’t finish before I arrived, and I went straight to the eye section of the hospital for the follow up field of vision test to see if last week’s lower than normal score was reflexes or an actual change in my vision. I passed this time, so this is now three times, I think, where I have been called back a few days for a do-over of that test, and did better the second time.
A good workday and a kindrid spirit
Then I went to work and met with some colleagues for help on a project, and after lunch I went to a meeting to be interviewed for a paper on how people interact with data and meta data in an era of “data driven science”, and discovered a kindrid spirit.
Fatemeh loves meta data as much as I do, and we had a great discussion on databases, science  what is data, what is metadata, etc. We also discussed the SCA, Visby medieval week, crafts, etc., and I promised to send links, which I did on the bus home.
Time to splat on the couch
Keldor and I made it home at the same time today, literally. He picked me up from the side of the road as I was walking from the bus.
We were both feeling tired, and just wanted to curl up on the couch with food and a book.
So I warmed some left over veg and enjoyed it and read, as he installed the replacement water pump for his aquarium he’d bought today to replace the one thst broke yesterday (and, since he’d like to keep the fish alive, this was higher on the priority list than relaxing, for which I am certain that if the fish knew, they would be grateful).
But as soon as that was accomplished he went to make some popcorn, the perfect sit on the couch and relax sort of snack, and discovered to his dismay that we are nearly out of popcorn, and there isn’t even a single serving in the jar. So we went off to the store to get more, and, since we were there got some bananas, strawberries, and carrots, too  and even an low alcohol beer for him to enjoy with his popcorn.
He popped a big batch, and I took some in a smaller bowl with some nutritional yeast, and he took the rest in the huge bowl, with some spices, and we happily read for a while.
Home improvements
Evenually, he got sleepy and curled up on the couch for a nap, and I got up, washed the dishes, and went downstairs to paint a coat of wetroom primer paint over the wetroom wallpaper on the new wall in the bathroom.
Change in plans
We had planned to head to Luleå tomorrow directly after work for the first night of Spelmansstämman. This would have meant my heading in with him in the morning, and working at his dad’s till he was done.
But when we saw how tired we were after work today, and thought about how much I would meed to pack tonight, to be able to go tomorrow  we revised the plan.
I will work from home, he will go to work, and come home afterwards. We will enjoy a quiet evening at home, and then head north early Saturday sp I get there on time to join Danskul for one of their dances during the performance.

Journal/2026/2026-06-June/2026-06-12-it-.filePath: Journal/2026/2026-06 June/2026-06-12 it took half a day to truly wake up, but then it was full speed ahead.md
Journal/2026/2026-06-June/2026-06-12-it-.title: 2026-06-12 it took half a day to truly wake up, but then it was full speed ahead
Journal/2026/2026-06-June/2026-06-12-it-.content:
procrastination
A very slow starting day, I was sleepy when we woke, and stayed tired for hours. Instead of working I found myself procrastinating with useful tasks that have nothingto do with work, like updating GnuCash with the money I spent while travelling.
Eventually, I ate lunch and took a short nap on the couch. When I woke I contemplated just calling it a sick day.
suddenly productive
So I sat at the computer, saw the file my colleague gave me, and started making a report of the terms that appear in the “species” column of the data set, which ones are for plants and animals already in the database, and which are new, and what terms are neither plant nor animal, and we might consider a different column for that info.
Before I knew it, I was 100% focused on working, taking careful notes about what and how. By the time I noticed being tired again I had accomplished 8.5 hours of actual work. (Keldor had gotten home long before, and had bern naping in front of a movie.)
the rest of the evening
After putting down the computer, I helped Keldor unload the four new concrete pillar bases he bought second hand today. That brings us to nine total (the others we bought second hand last year), so we may have enough for the deck now.
Then I took a little time to relax before yoga. The cats helped.

Now it is nearly 23:00, and I had better pack my folk dance stuff and get some slerp, so we can hit the road early tomorrow.

Journal/2026/2026-06-June/2026-06-13-a-g.filePath: Journal/2026/2026-06 June/2026-06-13 a glimpse of Spelmansstämman.md
Journal/2026/2026-06-June/2026-06-13-a-g.title: 2026-06-13 a glimpse of Spelmansstämman
Journal/2026/2026-06-June/2026-06-13-a-g.content:
This morning we drove up to Luleå, arriving to Gammelstad just after 10:00. Keldor dropped me off at the parking area, and I had just time to go to the loo and to change into my folk costume (I didn’t see any point in wearing it for a two hour drive), before the day’s opening procession began. In all previous years I have attended I have walked with this procession, so it was interesting to watch it coming, instead, and I even remembered that I own a camera, and that it will do films. I have made no attempt at editing it, but if you want a glimpse of that part of my day, here it is.


After filming that, and chatting with a few people, I joined the people in Danskul for a quick rehearsal of our performance, and was delighted to be recruited for two additional dances over and above the one I had planned on. After rehearsal we had a bit of time to relax and chat before it was our turn on the stage. The performance was fun, I love dancing!
Then I chatted with a few more people, till the series of dance workshops started. They were all at beginner level, but all dancing is fun, so I joined them for every set. Each workshop was 30 minutes, and had a different teacher.
First Helena ran a set of easy dances for children and adults, then Caroline taught basic Schottis, followed by Eva’s Rundpolska set, David’s Vals workshop, and finally Elisabet’s Kadril course.
After the Kadril I called Keldor, who was out at the smithy and let him know things were wrapping up, and I was ready to be picked up. thinking that we would do stuff together, either I would join them at the smithy, or something else till time for the evening dance at 20:00. However, he heard that I was ready to go home, so he finished what he was doing, packed up his things, and came and got me, arriving just after the final performance on the main stage ended.
I was a bit surprised that he was thinking of heading home, when we had talked about staying for the evening dance, but it wasn’t hard to convince me, either, and we were back to Skellefteå on by 18:00, stopped by the store to pick up some groceries, and were home by 18:42. Then he soaked in the tub, while I cooked a pot of chili to enjoy tomorrow.
Now I think I will go cuddle with him a bit, do my yoga, and see if I can get to bed at a reasonable hour.

It turns out that it also fits me, and a really, really high percentage of people I have helped with costumes over the years since, so I just keep reusing it.

Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-01-May-.title: 2026-05-01 May day holiday at home
Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-01-May-.content:
Today, the cats relaxed and took naps, After Anna & Jonas and their quiet dog, who had dropped by this morning, headed  towards home. (The dog was so quiet that Kali actually nearly walked up to it. I think, given a longer visit, they have a chance to get on friendly terms.)

We, in contrast, were busy.
My accomplishments include mixing a new batch of Muesli, fixing the lid on one of the bentwood boxes, doing the paperwork for the shire’s income form yesterday’s sales of burgers and snacks at the Valborg celebration, setting up the geteld that we fixed in March to be certain that the new poles Keldor made for it are the right size (they are), and make note of the holes to be mended.
I also tried to make a modification to my Camping loo, a bit of foam in the wooden lid that will hold the ceramic lid of the chamber pot in place, but the lid was too thick, so I undid it, and decided to do without.
In The evening Þórólfr and Caspian came over snd Keldor helped Þórólfr get started on his banner, and I helped Caspian start a new pair of SCA trousers. The kid turns 14 next week, and has outgrown most of his garb. We cut the legs full width of fabric, so they can have a long hem that can be let out later.
Keldor made a new knife handel today, with a bit of dinosaur bone in it.

Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-03-doub.title: 2026-05-03 double wars prep at the workshop
Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-03-doub.content:
Today we came into town, did some grocery shopping, bought some silk from Sofie, and then went to Keldor’s work workshop,  where he started building a spit roast grill, so that we can roast the wild pig his brother in law hunted, on Thursday night at Double Wars.

While he did that I washed the car and put a long-needed silver outline on my “rainbow” Laurel wreath on the hood.(When we bought the paint fot it, we couldn’t find a good heraldic green, or purple at the local stores, so went with a darker green than optimal, and the only purple we found was a “metalic” purple, which has, oddly, faded to a cyan/turquoise blue, so while it still reads as kinda rainbow, it isn’t a proper rainbow without purple. We did look again today for green and purple paint, but still no good options, so I am ignoring the problem.)

After doing that I sanded away all of the winter’s new rust spots, added some zinc paint to, hopefully stop them from rusting again, and then covering with black paint. While waiting for the zinc to dry, I cleaned and vacuumed the car, so now it will be a nicer space to spend 15 to 20 hours while driving south.
However, as I was driving home the car started shaking a little, so I stopped in a parking pull-off and checked the tires. The left rear tire rim was very hot (and only that rim). Keldor was about 10 minutes behind me in his work car, so I waited until he arrived (the rim was still hot). He drove my car home, so he could listen, but, of course the problem didn’t reoccur during that final 15 minutes of the trip, and tire rim was not hot when he arrived. I will try calling the local shop in the morning to see if they have time to look at it before we leave on Thursday.

Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-04-it-m.title: 2026-05-04 it may not be a problem at this time
Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-04-it-m.content:
Called the shop in Ånäset at 07:00, they don’t have time between now and Thursday to look at the car, but from my description, he guesses that it was a break that got stuck somehow, and he recommends driving it and seeing if the problem comes back. Since I finally got the dataset we have been waiting for for months at work, we decided that rather than spending time calling around to find someone to look at it today, I would work, and after work we will try a test drive and see. Worst case scenario we look into borrowing a car and hiring a trailer for the trip south.
After work I drove into town, with no symptoms of any car problems, so he checked the oil and changed a headlight, and a few other useful tasks,  and I drove home again (still no car problems, so we will hope it is ok enough for the drive south on Tuesday).
He stayed at the workshop and finished the spit roasting grill.

Which packs so compactly that he says “Ikea are amateurs”.

I had enough energy when I got home to make a batch of berry almond mousse ice cream, and, having bought a bag of kale yesterday, and dried it overnight, I also filled a jar with my Instant soup blend, this time, since we were nearly out of mushroom powder I took the coarse bits of dried mushrooms (that didn’t go through the sive the last time I made and sifted mushroom powder from dried mushrooms) and ran them through the mini food processor, which quickly turned it to powder. Since it was out, I put each sub batch of the ingredients in the mini food processor too, so it is well blended.
Then I filled my various wooden boxes with nuts, seeds, and dried fruit, and I filled the new little wicker basket with some spice jars,  so my event pantry is packed with the basics. Hopefully I will find the energy to bake oatcakes, flatbred, and cookies between now and Thursday when we leave.

Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-05-Rörm.content:
Luckily, I worked from home today, as the plumbers finally returned to install the toilet and sink in the attic. They had said that they should be able to do so sometime last week or this before we head south for Double Wars, but I hadn’t heard a revised estimate of when before Niklas just showed up. Since one of the things he will be doing is running the water pipe from the cellar to the attic through the closet area next to the bathroom on the main floor I moved the box of cat sand out from the bottom of that space and vacuumed so that he will have more pleasant access to the space. When he is done we can re-install the shelves in the cupboard and move the towels and cleaning supplies back. However, there is also lots of packing to do for Double Wars, so I don’t know if I will get to it. I hope that I do, it would be much nicer for the cat sitters if that is done, as it would be easier to find that stuff there, than in the temporary storage areas we have been using since the closet was dismantled on 2026-01-28 a busy morning.
The project has taken not quite five months from the day the contractor started building the walls for the attic loo to transforming the space to a usable loo. It would have gone much faster if we hadn’t done much of the work ourselves, in between all of the hobbies, work, and social life.

Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-07-förs.title: 2026-05-07 första del av resan till Dubblekriget
Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-07-förs.content:
I woke at 03:14 and got up and started loading the car. With the addition of my Camping loo we have a box that didn’t exist last tourney season,  and we are bringing pavilions for others in the camp, so even though we sent some stuff in Þórólfr’s trailer, it was necessary to do some careful tetris to get the boxes arranged under the bed, with room behind them for most of the pavilion poles. Then I got all the tents into the car  and decided I should take a nap, so I got 40 minutes more sleep snuggled up to Keldor before his alarm went off.
So we got up, and he drove to town to pick up his cousin, who is staying with the cats while we are at Double Wars, and I worked for a short while.
After they were hone I wrapped up what I was doing on the computer and started packing the ice chests, pillows, and other last minute things, while he put the table, bench, and long tent poles onto the roof rack.
We finally started driving at 13:09, about two hours later than he had hoped, and about two hours earlier than I feared (I choose not to bake the crackers I had wanted to bake, to pull this off. But I will regret that when I don’t have them on site. At least I baked oatcakes and cookies yesterday).
During the drive we reviewed a paper on Viking Swords for Complete Anchronist.
At 15:20, when we were somewhere south of Nordmaling, I posted to our group chat:  “We were just passed by a guy driving well over the speed limit in order to just slip in front of us before the passing lane ended, as as we heard the “woosh” of the car’s passing we both laughed at . the “Highway to Hell” sign that covers the full width of the back window. Yup, the car went by like a bat out of hell, in a hurry to get home!”
To make it even funnier, the letter part of its license plate is ONS, which stands for onsdag (Wednesday), so no wonder it drives so fast, today is Thursday, and it is late!
We stopped at the rest stop at 17:30 ish at Högakustenbrön, where I did some yoga. Then we continued south and picked up Charlotte at the big Y(sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Y:et).
I took a nap for 25 minutes, and otherwise enjoyed the company, and wildlife viewing (a cute long beaked bird, a wild piglet (or as Keldor calls it, “bacon seed”) and a hare, all in fairly quick succession), getting to Keldor’s brother’s house just before midnight.

Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-08-day-.filePath: Journal/2026/2026-05 May/2026-05-08 day two of the journey to Double Wars.md
Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-08-day-.title: 2026-05-08 day two of the journey to Double Wars
Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-08-day-.content:
We reached Robert’s just enough before midnight that we were back on the road four minutes before midnight, which gave us just enough time to chat a little, pick up the  things we’d come to collect, and borrow the toilet.
Then it was “only” 199 km left to drive to their sister’s house where the bed was already standing ready for our arrival.
We arrived at Rebeccah’s at 02:30, and went straight to bed. Keldor woke feeling refreshed around 08:30. I was still super tired, but as we had sat in a car for 12 hours yesterday, I did a quick pilates session, and then slept another hour.
When I woke I checked the gps, and it said if we left now, we would be at site at 14:30. I didn’t want to get up, but we wanted to visit at least one runestone on the way, so I did.
It turned out that Rebeccah had gotten up a bit before me, and was mixing up a batch of scones. So we spent a pleasant not quite two hours chatting over breakfast, and started driving towards site at 11:30.
If all had gone well, and there were no reasons to stop, that would have gotten us to site at 16:11, which would be quite ok timing, as from 16:00 one can drive in and start setting up camp.
A bit after 13:00 Charlotte suggested we stop at a pharmacy, as she needed something to treat the pain in her tummy/gallbladder. A bit later she realised that the pain was migrating, and the symptoms were now more like a heart attack (she has had two previously), so we dialed the gps to the nearest emergency room, which was in Hässleholm, about 40 minutes away.
Her pain got worse, so we called emergency services (112 in Sweden), and after describing the symptoms they suggested we pull over and wait for an ambulance to come to us. Luckily, just about then there was a gas station at the side of the road, so we could wait under its roof, at which point we were 30 minutes from the emergency room we had been aiming at.
It took about 30 minutes for the ambulance to arrive and check her out. The first person got out, and introduced themselves to Charlotte “Hi, my name is Emma”. The the driver got out and came over, and I read the driver’s name tag. Emma. Yes, they are both Emma, makes it easier they said.
They decided to bring her into the hospital, and we started driving towards site again. Revised ETA, if we don’t stop, 17:45.
As it turned out, we managed to arrive on site at 17:40. After checking in we unloaded the car (with pauses on Keldor’s part to discuss camp laout plans with the others now that the full extent of our land allotment is known, and I kept unloading and sorting stuff into related piles for easier finding later).
By the time the car was empty the plan was complete, so I started putting up my Pavilion while Keldor took the car to the parking lot.  He was back by the time I needed help, and then I started moving in while he set up other tents.
It was full dark by the time the tents were done, so the sunshades needed to wait for tomorrow. He sat down and ate something our camp mates fed him, while I finished enough of the moving in and organising of stuff that I was starting to think perhaps it was bed time.
About then he came in to get his toothbrush,  so I accepted that it was, did a short yoga session, and we were in bed before midnight (15 minutes before counts).

Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-09-the-.filePath: Journal/2026/2026-05 May/2026-05-09 the camp is up.md
Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-09-the-.title: 2026-05-09 the camp is up
Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-09-the-.content:
Clearly I didn’t drink enough water during camp set up yesterday, as I didn’t need to test my new Camping loo, and slept for almost 8 hours. Normally that much time would need at least two trips to the loo!
We spent the morning setting up the sunshades, tables, shelves, banners, etc, to make the camp comfortable and welcoming.

Then I spent the rest of the day being socialbe, or useful, or both.
While talking with others who don’t conform to the traditional gender spectrum, I coined a new term, nontrinary, which I feel beautifully describes how I feel about my gender, so far from the traditional binary scale that one needs a third axis to show how I am not on it. My pronouns could therefore be they/them/it.
I went up to the hall around 23:00 to do my yoga, but my phone battery died mid-session, so I went back to the tent, got my charger, and the second try with the app was successful.

Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-10-Casp.title: 2026-05-10 Caspians AoA
Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-10-Casp.content:
I got to bed at 02:00, and was grateful to have the hot water bottle, as I had gotten rather cold even sitting in the hall talking to Maggie, Madelenia, and others after yoga.
At 04:00 I was woken by a Keldor-sized block of ice that crawled into bed, so I put the still kinda warm (but way, way warmer than him) hot water bottle between us in self defense and tried to warm him, without touching his arms, which were even colder than his body. Of course, the non-commutative ice-block kept trying to put those cold arms against my warm body. Poor thing.
After he had warmed up to tepid I left the blankets long enough to pee, and then curled back up with him and slept till 09:30, when he woke needing to head to the loo.
I woke to notifications on my phone, one of which opened FB, where I saw a post by Countess Agness showing various Pride flags, and offering to make necklaces in those colours if people are interested.
I would be, but the ones that aren’t rainbow that could apply to me are in colour schemes that don’t appeal to me. I need to design a nontrinary flag in colours that I like, and then see if anyone else feels like they could identify that way.
I took the day as a relax and be social in camp day, and didn’t attend any official  activities other than court.
The camp had one miss adventure. I had just returned from filling my water picture and placed it on the table, when suddenly the bench upon which Þórólfr was sitting made a loud cracking noise, and the back support fell, and he fell backwards, feet rising up, which knocked the table sowly over, causing everything on it to slide to the ground.
Luckily, he wasn’t hurt, and nothing on the tabel broke, though my water picture is chipped. Keldor fixed the broken bench an hour or so layer when he returned to camp.
I helped Petronlia fix the fitting of a wool over dress, and helped Erin mark and cut the hem on her skirt. I started also hemming the skirt, till Felicitas complained about having eyelets to sew,  and I volunteered to trade projects. So during court I sewed lacing point eyelets in the tops of felicitas’s new hose, and Felicitas worked on Erin’s hem.
Pre-court entertainment was, of course, the reading of the Knäckebröd war story. Then followed Court for both Drachenwald and Nordmark, with one full dozen Royal and Baronial crowns in attendance.
For our camp the highlight was an Award of Arms to Lord Caspian, who celebrated his 14th birthday the day before, but there were many other well deserved awards.
Beig tired, I did my yoga not so long after court, and Keldor and I both went to bed around 23:00.

Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-11-a-ra.title: 2026-05-11 a rainy day
Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-11-a-ra.content:
Despite having gotten to bed by midnight, I had trouble getting up in the morning. I woke several times, ranging from super early, through early, to “really ought to get up”,  but each time I would think about getting up, perhaps do some yoga, or get a shower, or something, yet I fell back to sleep each time.
I finally got up just on time to attend Erik Hane’s class on kydex armour, where we adjusted the fitting of the legs Keldor had ordered for me. It rained lightly then, but didn’t seem very cold. However, as the day progressed, the rain and cold both intensified. To further complicate the morning, there was no running water in camp for a few hours this morning.
I spent some time in camp at the fire being socialbe, and some time in the hall sewing and being socialbe, plus attending choir practice, so I managed to finish both Erin’s skirt hem, and Felicitas’ hose lasing points.
Choir was fun. We started with drinking songs that are rounds, so everyone singing the same melody. When we switched to parts, the first song was Gaudete, which song I have known the melody of forever, but I couldn’t remember the alto line (I know we sung it in the Student Choir Aurora,  where they put me with the altos). When Natfari demonstrated all of the parts I, and one other, decided to go join the tennors, as their part sounded easier. Besides (insert name) from Germany was with the tennors to help them (but could have sung with any of the voices), and is super easy to follow.
After choir I helped carry out the animals for Thursday’s 3D archery shoot, followed by taking a sheepskin and the hot water botthes up to the hall intending to do a quick yoga, fill the bottles and leave them in bed and then head up to soak in the hotbtub for the first time this event.
Instead, my phone struggled to download a yoga session. I eventually managed to get an 8 minutes session,  and then, since Aud and Tyra had joined me for it, did even more yoga and conversation,  followed by an impromptu dance session with them. Then I finally got to the part about putting the hot water bottles into bed, and the bed looked so inviting I returned to the hall to let Aud know I was skipping the hottub in favour of sleep. I also stopped by the gaming party at Sven and Siobhan’s to say goodnight to Keldor before laying down and typing up the last of the day

Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-12-bard.title: 2026-05-12 bardic!
Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-12-bard.content:
Midnight weirdness
I went to bed just after midnight, and woke a bit after 02:00, when Keldor came in, so I got up and went to the loo and returned to bed.
I woke again at just after 03:00, when Keldor got up. It was very dark in the tent. I started to fall back asleep, but then thought I should drink some water, so I turned on the light on my phone to find my water bottle,  and was surprised to find Keldor standing on my side of the bed, reaching for me.
I asked what he was doing, and he replied that he was looking for me, a d tried to crawl into bed, head towards the foot end of the bed. I pointed out he was on the wrong side of the bed, a d he said he was looking for the bed, so I told him to go around everything his own side (the headboard of the bed is up against the center pole,  against which we have shelves and chests), and I shined my phone light to show him the path.
That is when I saw the large puddle of liquid on the tent floor, and more liquid flowing away from the puddle across my carpet. The one ni e wool carpet that had cone to the event in our car, and so didn’t get soaked in lamp oil in Þórólfr’s trailer on the way to the event.
Knowing there was nothing in the tent contsining liquid he could have knocked over and spilled on the floor, I asked him “did you pee in the tent?”, to which he replied “ingen aning” (No idea). Yah, I belive that part. I have no idea what he had to drink last night, nor how much, but I cannot recommend it, as it makes it possible to get lost trying to leave the tent and pee on the canvas floor.
I tried to ignore the problem and go back to sleep, the damage already being done, and still being very tired, but I was too bothered by it all, and failed to sleep. So I got back up, turning on the light to see that the liquit had now soaked into the wool carpet, so I put the terry cloth towel down over the wet spot, so I wouldn’t step on it, and went to the loo.
since I wasn’t sleeping
I decided I may as well do my yoga for the day, and see if that helped, so I went back to the tent  got my phone and a sheepskin to tske to the hall, and decided that I may as well get some water bottles to refill.
As I gathered all of that Keldor got up, pulled on his sauna tunic, stumbled, barefoot, out of the tent, and started stagering towards the loo. I walked with him, and tried to steer him towards the hall, where I could put my stuff down as he used the toilet, and then help him back to camp, but he insisted going to the outhouses.
So I dropped my stuff off in the hall, and went back out on time to see hom returning, shivering. So I helped him back to bed, got him covered and put a nålbinded slipper on one of his feet (I couldn’t find the other), and pulled the still warmer than his feet hot water bottle near his feet.
The  I did a half hour training,fulled my watter bortles, typed the above, and returned to bed a bit after 05:00.
after second sleep
We both woke a bit before 10:00, and I asked him how he was feeling, and he said fine. I asked if he remembered anything about last night, or more specifically this morning, and he replied “only a vauge feeling of panic”.  So I told him the above story, and he replied “Jag är så ledsen” (I am so sorry).
He doesn’t remember any of that, and when asked what he had to drink, he remembers only the three beers he took with him to the sauna. He had nothing resembling a hangover this morning, and wonders if he had simply been sleep walking.
We will probably never know if he accepted something stronger than his beers, and it was drunkeness that caused the problem, or if it was sleep walking related.
But we both woke feeling great, and our camp quickly accomplished our assigned camp chores for the day. He and Alfarinn took care of replacing the marshlights, I and Þórólfr cleaned the dishwashing station by the hall, and some of the Frostheim folk (I didn’t see which ones) took care of the pots and pans dishwashing station.
afternoon
I got my massge at noon, and then went to choir practice, a little late. Today I sang with the tenors the whole time. They had gotten to Gaudete by the time I arrived, and there were only three tennors today, so I joined them, but without our strong lead it was harder, until I turned to face behind the other tenors, pointing one hearing aid outside the ring, and one towards the tennors, so they were easier to hear (and my mouth war pointed away, so that if I was wrong I wouldn’t take them with me).but then Martin, who was in armour, took a pause from pickups to come sing with us. Martin has a strong, beautiful voice, and sings tennors, so we could easily follow him, and one of the ladies who had been singing tennor only because we were so few could go back to the altos, which meant that another, who had been singing alto because they were fewer than the sopranos could also move back up to her preferred range.
After choir I stopped by the fighting, brought Keldor some snacks and drinks and chatted with a few fighters before heading to Lucie’s class on the decorations on Skolderhamn outfit. When she got to the embroidery on the legs of the trousers she explained rhat it wasn’t quite right as the yarn she used was too thick. So I asked if she had found a better yarn when she dud Keldor’s, and she had, so I fetched them for her to pass around. After the presentation she had sime yarn for thosevif us who want to, to try some of the braids. I did the 6-strand (double thread in each) three colour braid, which I have done before  years ago, at the Tromsø museum, when I was there for Þhora’s lecture on her weaving of the Skjdoleham cloak fabric. I had forgotten making that, till the braid started coming together.
Bardic
Then I was starving so returned to canp to eat, tidy up, and rearrange furniture for the bardic.
By 19:00, which was the advertised start time for the bardic, we had a nice set up of benches and chairs around the double fire pits, and a few of us who live here, and a couple from Styringheim, which was enough to start the singing. I took the smaller of the two camp chainmail-wearing teddybears as the designated turn marker to pass around the circle, which worked very well.
We managed a couple of circuits around the small circle before others joined is and filled out the space. It was an amazing evening that made me very happy. We had a few people with a large repertoire to hop in when the bear-holder had a request, and most people participated.
We had lots of sing-along pieces, with enough voices to make it sound good. We had performance pieces by onevor two, we had storytelling, poetry, and even a dramatic reading of the ingredients on abpacket of tea (which was fablous). We did period songs, SCA orginals, filks, modern songs with the right feeling, nd more. We sang in at least seven languages over the course of the evening, and I had so much fun that I didn’t want to leave for the loo, putting it off longer than was comfortable, so I only had to leave twice. Once in the middle of the evening, and again sometime after 01:00, when the circle had shrunk to only eight of us. While I was gone Felicitas recited a poem thst was so funny it broke Torunn to the piing where whe packed away her songbooks and when the bear returned to her she said she was done. We were all feeling tired and satisfied, so we chatted a bit longer, then the guests said goodnight, and we who lived here tidied upa little, put out the lights, and spread out the coals to slowly finish burning down, and I was in bed before 02:00.

Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-13-Wedn.title: 2026-05-13 Wednesday
Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-13-Wedn.content:
After yesterday’s nice weather all day yesterday, it felt a little disappointing to wake to rain, though it was nice to sleep in. Keldor went into town to buy more ice for the ice box with the now thawing wild boar for tomorrow’s grill party, and I had breakfast before heading over to the cabins so I could give a massage in payment for yesterday.
Then I had time to eat before heading to the Laurel Sponsored Prize Display (LSPD), after which I was going to head to Choir,  as was Aud, but Tyra had just returned from there saying that they had already given up for the day, as only four people showed up, including the director. I didn’t look at my phone, but I assume from this that the LSPD ran late.
So I wandered over to see some of the Claw of Drachenwald tournament. This was a tournament sponsored by some of the squires, who wanted to see their knights fighting their best and showing how it is done, with no consequences of a job if they win. So they invited all knights (and only knights) to a tournament, with a rotating prize, that the winner wll pass on to next year’s winner.
Keldor was one of the artists to make the prize. He forged a steel cup/chalice, with a bit of meteorite in the base. Then he sent it to Styringheim, where Baron John Smith added bling in the form of a gold interior and gold decoration bits on the outside.
I watched some of the fighting, and chatted with some people. At one point Attli had a problem with one of the strips of extra fabric on his fighting trousers breaking loose and the Marshall needing to tie them out of the way.
Therefore,  after the tournament I took Attli’s trousers to mend as my sew during court project, for which I received many thanks.

Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-14-mark.filePath: Journal/2026/2026-05 May/2026-05-14 market day-wild pig roasting-great court.md
Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-14-mark.title: 2026-05-14 market day-wild pig roasting-great court
Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-14-mark.content:
We got up around 08:00 and Keldor started getting his wild pig onto the spit roast, and I helped Erich Hane set up his tent for the market for several of us to share.
Then I went to laurel meeting followed by spending the day at market,  where I sold some of Sorkar och Strängar’s songbooks, one bodkin arrowhead and a couple of belt hooks.
I also helped Erin do her shopping by paying Swish for a few of her purchases, and then she sent me a single Wise transfer to cover it.
By the time I had packed up the merchant tent Keldor’s pig was nearing the appropriate temperature for eating, and a few people were sitting and chatting with him as he continued to brush it with melted butter (and sometimes honey). Every so often he would rotate it a little more, and keep feeding the fire to keep it at just the right level to cook without burning.
As he cooked, I sat and helped Felicitas with mending venetian trousers, but it didn’t look like the trousers would be usable on time for court, which was a shame, as Felicitas was to attend the Prince and Princess of Insulae Draconis at court.
Then someone noiced the blue flashing lights of an ambulance up by the hall, and a bit later Daniel, who lives in our camp, came by,  looking very shaken, to say that there was a medical emergency and that the area near the hall was closed while emergency services dealt with it.
We made the assumption that this would cause a delay in court and I continued to mend the trousers as Felicitas mended the doublet.
Since the nature of the emergency wasn’t stated I was curious which end of the spectrum it was on, remembering various deaths and accidents at SCA events that  I have heard of over the years ranging from sudden heart failure to freak accident/injury, to carbon monoxide poisoning in a well-sealed modern tent. I hoped that today’s emergency was a solvable problem, preferably one that stemed from medical issues already present in one individual human, and not from someone making a mistake that had severe and painful consequences for more than one individual.
Eventually word went out that yes, court would be delayed, probably by around an hour, and Keldor kept basting the pig, and Felicitas and I kept sewing.
As a result, I managed to finish darning the waistband fabric and reconstrusting the waistband where the original metal eyelets had catastrophically failed, and even got the first new eyelet half done before the call for people to assemble for court went around.
At this point Felicitas got dressed in the now much better, but still not fully mended, clothing, and I gathered my nålbindning project in progress (Blue handwarmers),  put on my warm outer layers (including my Viking Cloak) , grabbed a ground cloth to sit on (the day having been sunny, the ground was dry again), my mug of water, a bow for the cermony, gave Keldor a smooch, and left him on pig roasting duty and went to court.
Court opened with Tyndal, Drachenwald’s Seneschal, making the somber announcement that yes, there has been a medical emergency, that an individual had been found in their room breathing but unresponsive, the medics on site and an ambulance were summoned, and the individual had been transported to the hospital accompanied by their family. No further information is available at this time. Out of respect for them and their family, please refrain from spreading rumours and speculations.
Then court itself started with Siobhan’s Pelican ceremony, which included a very nice variation on calling the speakers for the canidate. Instead of mentioning what each order is known for, and how a peer of this order must also embody that trait and then pausing as a speaker for one order is called forward to do a speech, and then continuing with the litany “the order ___ is known for ___ , but  ___ , too must also embody ___ ” For the next speaker/order, the herald read the entire section in one go, without pauses, and then called for speakers, starting with the populace, who came up, made a beautiful and touching speach, and then stood to the side, carrying a sign with a symbol of the people and an “e”. Then each speaker in turn came up, did their short speeches, and then joined the line of speakers, holding up a sign with a letter and the symbol of their order.
E
CE
ICE
VICE
RVICE
ERVICE
SERVICE
I really liked this approach, as it felt quicker than the traditional approach, and watching a word form, one letter at time, backwards, added an additional level of interest for the audience.
I, for one, had fun thinking of a number of words that end with the letters already revealed and how they  are or are not apt for the canidate (the combination of letters “vice” seemed especially apt for a peer who regularly hosts gambling nights in camp).
Court then swithed over to Nordmark, who presented some well deserved awards and acknowledged other good things before it swithed back to Drachenwald, who had a few more pieces of business, including gifts to the children and welcoming newcomers, of whom I had spent quality time with at least five if the ten or so who came up.
Then the archers were summoned to make an honour guard arch to welcome Alys to court for the beautiful cermony to become Drachenwalds third Premier member of the order of the mark.
After court people gathered in our camp to sample roasted wild pig, and many other good foods provided by our friends and enjoy quiet conversation.
Later in the evening the Seneschal dropped by with the sad news that her Excellency didn’t make it, which will be hard on everyone in Drachenwald, but especially her family and local group.
Sometime quite late I left our gathering to go soak in the hot tub for a bit, came back, chatted a while  did some yoga, chatted some more, and went to bed a bit after 02:00.

Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-15-Nord.filePath: Journal/2026/2026-05 May/2026-05-15 Nordmarks furstinna fyller år.md
Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-15-Nord.title: 2026-05-15 Nordmarks furstinna fyller år
Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-15-Nord.content:
I slept in till 09:30, and then made breakfast. There being left over Finnish squeaky cheese  from last night, I cooked up a yummy curry for breakfast, using that cheese, the last of my spinach, some nettles, and some of my Instant soup blend. After I had eaten, Keldor claimed the leftovers to start a stew, to which he added the  left over wild pig from last night, and to which the others in the camp added the vegetables they hadn’t yet cooked, and even some beef found its way in the pot. They wound up with a big enough batch that everyone in our camp, and a few visitors, got some, and there was still some stew in the pot.
While they started the stew, I went up to choir, and enjoyed singing, especially after Etienne joined the tennors for Turdion, and again when Martin joined us for Come Again. It is nice when there is a strong tenor to follow.
Then back to camp, where we did a little pre-packing that won’t need doing tomorrow, including taking apart the big plywood insulated box the frozen wild pig had travelled in. I leaned the plywood pieces against the tree for the bit of ice melt water to dry out of it.
Then it was time for court, where the biggest award was an argumentation of arms for Margaret de May, especially for her work founding the Drachenwald Law Council.
Alas, choir didn’t get to perform before or during court, which was disappointing. I asked the herald later, and they were trying to save time, but they could have accomplished that by having us sing before court, instead of having us “in reserve”, as possible entertainment if a runner needed to be sent for someone.
Durring court the Princess of Nordmark announced that she was having a birthday party that evening,  but I had a hint of something that could be a sore throat coming on, so I skipped the party (not wanting to share if I was getting sick), and went to bed before 22:00. Keldo, being tired, joined me.
Previous post: 2026-05-14 market day-wild pig roasting-great court

Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-16-on-b.title: 2026-05-16 on battery alone
Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-16-on-b.content:
packing
I got up at 05:00 to start packing, and by the time Keldor woke at around 07:00 I had managed to get the food and ice chests repacked into “want in reach while driving”, and “don’t need to see till we are home”, likewise my sewing projects and clothing.
I had found and washed our scattered feast gear, though hadn’t packed that chest yet, as we had talked about cooking all of the eggs, it seems that many in camp had bought eggs, so there were more than a couple dozen left. However, no one in camp bothered building a fire, but each in turn got up and started packing. So I asked, and it was agreed I should put all the eggs in our big ice chest.
Keldor quickly packed his personal stuff and then went out to stsrt working on stuff in the common areas, as I started working on bedding. Bjarni was in camp wondering if there was a way to help as I got to the part about taking apart the rope bed, so I happily got their help/company with that step, passing the rope shuttle back and forth, unweaving the bed.
Then I could drop my tent, and all of the other tents in our camp were also down or ready to drop, and the gate was open to let people drive in.
Keldor focused on getting stuff on the roof rack that has to go there, I focused on getting things packed to fit in my car in more or less the same configuration as on the tip down. Meanwhile everyone else loaded the trailer and other cars, with pauses to say good-bye to others who were ready to go sooner than we were.
The site gates were only open for cars in the morning, up to 13:00, and the last Camp Northern Lights car (ours), rolled out the gate just before 13:00. Keldor parked in the parking lot and came back for a quick round of goodbyes etc.
driving
Keldor’s sister Ragna rode with us this time, as Charlotte is still in the hospital, and we were heading to her house to sleep tonight anyway.
We left site at 13:15. A short while later I remembered the second hand store we randomly stoped at on the way home last year, where he bought a cannon, so I asked google maps for second hand stores near our route.  The second one we tried wss the same store, but they had no cannons this time. I did get a pair of black jeans and a few blue glassplates.that might make good lids for my blue glass bowls.

car troubles
Some time after 16:00 a warning light on the car came on saying that the battery wasn’t charging (the same warning we had a year ago when a belt broke and we stayed extra days in Uppsala to get it fixed). We were about a half an hour from Värnamo, where there is a Biltema, so we hoped we would make it that far before stopping to look, and we did.
This time we saw no obvious problem, so we bought a backup battery, and a tool to read the current level of charge on the battery (about 12 volts), and we continued toward Vadstena.
Sometime later Felicitas posted in the group camp chat about being home, and so tired that emotions were numb, which meant that post-event blues hadn’t hit yet, to which I replied:

Our post event blues have been put asside for the game “will the car make it to Vadstena on battery power alone?“

reaching Vadstena
We did make it to her house, but instead of sewing we spent the driving time looking at options. It being a Saturday evening, there is no way we will get a workshop to look at the car today or tomorrow, but we need to be home on time to pick up the cat sitter from the airport on Tuesday before taking our Wednesday morning flight to Ireland. (Since Keldor’s armour traveled home in Þórólfr’s trailer, we can’t just have someone else pick up the cat sitter and change our booking to start the trip in Stockholm. )
Most options considered are to leave the car in Vadstena, let a shop fix it, and head home with just the stuff we need for the Ireland adventure. Then we could change the return flight to stop in Stockholm and pick up the car then.
alternatives considered
A one way rental car would cost at least 7000 kr, and the earliest available is Monday. A train costs at least 3000 kr, and the earliest available is Sunday evening.  There are a few used cars listed for around 10,000 kr, which would also solve the problem of Keldor’s current car is still broken. So this is the most appealing option for me.
We did send a a couple messages as we drove, to cars with a note with a varient of “cheaper for quick sale”. One replied right away saying they aren’t home this weekend, how about next? We replied we were only passing through, and aren’t here then.
an early night
We arrived at 20:50, I did my yoga as the others ate a late dinner, then took a shower and went to bed, though I stayed up updating my logs till 22:15.

Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-17-new-.filePath: Journal/2026/2026-05 May/2026-05-17 new day, new car.md
Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-17-new-.title: 2026-05-17 new day, new car
Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-17-new-.content:
I woke at 7:30 ish and finished updating my log from yeasterday. When I got to the bit about sending messages on used cars I realised I should check messages, and yes,
A reply came in during the night from the other car we messaged asking for an offer, so we sent one. No reply before Keldor managed to find an old Saab on FB marketplace.

Now we just need to repack and see if it will get us home.
First runestone stop
Runsten Nä11, L1980:4067, Stora Mellösa 80:1, Örebro, is a cute runestone built into a stone wall around someone’s house.

But I think I will need to trace it to figure out what the art is.

I was doing a video call with the person who will stay with the cats when I am in Ireland just as we arrived, so Aliçia got to be included in the selfie.

Second runestone stop
Runsten Nä12, L1981:8316, Stora Mellösa 32:1, Örebro
Is a lovely pink granite stone. There is another runestone inside the church, but it wasn’t open, so we missed that one.


and a treuddan
L1980:3563 Stora Mellösa 14:2
This is Närkes largest trident grave, an unusual grave form, with large stones marking a triangular boundry. This one dates to sometime between 800 to 1050 AD, so is at least 50 years younger than the church it sits next to.


Continuing north
The next real stop was in Sala, to buy icecream and snacks for the drive.

Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-18-and-.title: 2026-05-18 and home again
Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-18-and-.content:
Final bit of the drive
We drove till just after 01:00, and stopped at the Åhedån rest area, where we took a nap for 1 h 44 minutes. He sitting in the drivers seat, reclined, me curled up across some clothes pused between the two front seats, with my pillow on his tummy/chest. Not the most comfortable position, but it gave him enough rest to start driving again, with a revised estimate for home arrival at 04:20. This turned out to be a quite accurate prediction.
home again
I had just enough energy left to feed the cats, unload the stuff in the back seat, get food into the fridge, start a load of laundry in the machine in “delayed start” mode, so that it would finish in nine hours (in hopes that I would sleep so long), do yoga, and take a shower, which got me to bed at 05:37. Keldor, who had driven the full way, carried in one bag, and went straight to a shower and to bed.
I slept almost three hours, and Keldor woke and woke me. I went back to sleep for an hour, and then we got up.
glad we took the day off of work
We played a quick game of Qwirkle over breakfast, which I won, but we both had way lower scores than usual.
Then we put some stuff away, and I made a quick pot of soup. Thent it was time to deal with laundry, and I started another load, this time with a delayed start to be done in three hours, which I figured would be enough time to drive to Skelleftehamn to get our stuff that traveld in the trailer.
oops
Since we were there we also helped Þórólfr unload everything else in the trailer, too.
I carried one bag of coffee to the kitchen, set it on the table, turned quickly around and started walk quickly out of the room, tangled my feet on nothing, fell forward, tried catching myself with the other foot, hit a box with it, and fell faster, striking my forehead on the doorjam just before landing, hard, on my hands and knees. No breaks, but bruises on all five impact points. 100% do not recommend.
Needless to say, I took a break from unloading to hold some ice against my palms and forehead, but short attention span meant thst I was soon back to work.
In the evening Martin and Molly visited.
Got to bed at 00:13

Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-19-trav.title: 2026-05-19 travel prep
Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-19-trav.content:
We started the day with breakfast with Martin & Molly and then went to go look at the house they bought, which is a nice one. I hope they get renters soon.
After which Keldor drove to town to do errands for his dad, and pick up our cat sitter from the airport on the way home. My goal for the day is to pack our bags for flying to Ireland way too early tomorrow morning.
This goal was accomplished, but not without stress due to how many things that I needed, and used often at Double Wars, I had to leave at home due to baggage restrictions when one flys.
I even accomplished washing lots of loads of laundry, and re-washing a frying pan and a roasting pan that the cat sitter for Double Wars had put into the cupboard in a state that I found too icky to be there.
In between we got the cat sitter, Aliçia,  who is visiting from France, aquainted with where to find things in the house. I managed to do my at 22:30, and then the “last things” tasks were wrapped up so I could go to bed before midnight. Keldor was already fast asleep by then.

Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-20-firs.filePath: Journal/2026/2026-05 May/2026-05-20 first day Ireland visit.md
Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-20-firs.title: 2026-05-20 first day Ireland visit
Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-20-firs.content:
the flights
We set our alarm for 03:30, as Google told Keldor yesterday that airport security at Skellefteå Airport opens two hours before the flight. However, the sign on the side of the road outside the airport, by the closed gate, says one can’t drive onto airport land till one hour before the flight. We could have had another half hour of sleep before travel…
But all went smoothly with check-in after it was possible to come into the building.  The checked bags weigh 22.4 and 22.5 kg, which  since the limit is 23 kg, is good.
Our flight to Arlanda landed 25 minutes early, so we had oodles of time, which I should have spent sewing, but wound up scrolling for much of it. Oops. Eventually, we realised that while we were sitting by the gate, it never opened, so we checked, and they had switched gates.
So we went to the new gate, boatded, and around 2 hours later landed in Dublin a few minutes  early.
Ireland
Tania and Mike picked us up at the Dublin Airport and we drove the couple of hours out to their delightful stone cottage at Inistoige, where, after a very fast tour to introduce the place to Keldor, and show me the many improvements that have happened since I last visited, in 2010, we took a nap.
I woke after a half an hour, then enjoyed a snack and pleasant conversation with Tania and Mike.
the houses
Their stone cottage is really a collection of stone farm buildings around a courtyard which had sat vacant for around 30 years before they bought the place, and the bits that had been sheds and barns were in the worst shape when they got it, missing roofs and some walls.
The main house was in good enough shape that while they replaced the roof itself (and added skylights in the pricess) they were able to retain the original roof support beams.

Inside, the original fireplace was big enough to roast an ox, but now they use a wood stove instead.

We are staying in the nearly complete guest cottage, which has just this week gotten done enough to be usable. The last time I was here it, and the adjoining shed, had no roof, and no wall on one end (and walls that had crumbled some at the other three sides).
With the help of their friend Billy, who is tallented at stone work, both the uphill shed/workshop(left side), and the guest cottage (right side) now haave complete walls, with doors and windows, and a roof:

The wall at the end has fun decorations:

The door frame will be added soon. The guest bed has a glorious headboard that they have nearly finished restoring, but Mike’s emergency dental surgery a couple of days ago, followed by plumbing issues in the main house prevented the headboard being ready to attach before we arrived.
Given that we had gotten up at 03:30 to start our journey here, and had driven all day (and most of the night) the  before, we tryly didn’t care about the lack of the headboard, but went happily and went directly to sleep.
the orchard
After eating Tania took me out to see the orchard, which has five surriving big apple trees of the nine that were here when they bought the place 30 years ago.
Much of the orchard wall between the farm courtyard and the orchard still exists, but the bits surrounding the other three sides have nearly crumbled away.
Tania tells me that the biggest tree, which long ago fell, took new root, and started over, makes big glorious tart baking apples.

The one to the left grows smaller, yummy sweet eating apples that have a narrow window between ripe and gone. Someday she would like to try making cider from them.

Of course, most years, their touring cycle has them heading back to their home in Saquamish, Washington in the autumn, so usually it is the neighbours who come pick their apples after they are gone.
dinner
Keldor woke an hour or so after I did, an after repeating a quick version of the orchard tour we went in to the Green Spice Indian restaurant in Thomastown for dinner, arriving soon after their 5pm opening.
The food, as promised, was excellent, and the company, of course, better.
Thomastown castle and bridge
After dinner we walked over to the river to look at the town’s castle ruins:



and the nearby stone bridge:

And the view up the river:

Music
Then we returned to the house abd chatted for a bit before heading upstairs to practice a bit for their next consert.
While there she showed me the Seattle version of the Norrbotten polja tune Babba Lisas hyfs’n which they call “missing link” due to the pause that they so in the music, which she believes is not present in the original.
I tried playing her dulcimer a bit, but found it difficult without the colour coding I have painted on my bridges. Just as Tania found playing on mine challenging as it is harder to see the white and black bridges (that most dulcimer players uses for orientation points) with my colour coding.
However, I am feeling inspired to play dulcimer again, and even did a quick video of her playing, in hopes that it will help me learn it.
Previous post:  2026-05-19 travel prep

Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-21-a-lo.filePath: Journal/2026/2026-05 May/2026-05-21 a long walk followed by gaming night.md
Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-21-a-lo.title: 2026-05-21 a long walk followed by gaming night
Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-21-a-lo.content:
I went to bed just after 22:00 last night, and slept till just after 06:00, and lounged in bed nearly 2 hours updating logs and adding new music folders to my blog structure as Keldor slept, before getting up to do some yoga.
As I finished my yoga Billy was arriving to continue work on the cottage. This week’s project is removing the old layer of render that covers the stone of the main house, which will permit the stone to better breath, and make it last longer.
Sitting in that house and eating breakfast with Tania and Mike, we could hear the noise of the power tool coming through the window frame, though it wasn’t so bad as to really interfere with conversation, it would have been annoying to spend the whole morning listening to it.
However, when I went over to the guest cottage to check on Keldor to see if he was ready to get up for the day’s adventure, the sound was hardly noticeable, and he was still asleep.
A bit later he did get up, and he, Tania, and I took a walk down the to the village of Inistoige, and were out for three hours, returning to quiet  as Billy had finished work for the day.
I even sometimes remembered I had a camera, I so can present to you some horses in a field who were not the least interested in coming over to the fence to say hello:


 add the rest of the photos

After the walk we had soup for lunch and Keldor and I relaxed on the couch while Tania and Mike practiced for their upcoming concert (I love listening to them!)
Then we set up their new (used) solid oak table with a larger surface area than the one they had been using, and combined the tiles from two sets of Carcassonne, and played a couple of games. Mike warned us that they always win. He was right. However, in the first game I managed second place to Mike’s win. In the second game Tania beat Mike by three points, and I came in third. I really enjoy the game, as one can just focus on “what can I do to improve my own situation” and have fun, even when others are doing better. Much like my approach to life.
Previous post: 2026-05-20 first day Ireland visit

Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-22-Kell.title: 2026-05-22 Kells Priory visit
Journal/2026/2026-05-May/2026-05-22-Kell.content:
Morning
Woke up with enough energy to cross-post to Dreamwidth blog entries that got sent to my blog after Double Wars and before flying to Ireland, giving as an intro”

“Life before Double Wars was much too busy, and while I continued to record (some of) what I was up to in Obsidian, I didn’t manage to often push it to GitHub to my blog, and really didn’t manage to cross-post it here, though sometimes I managed to find time to read what you all were up to.
Today I finally feel like I have time to do a simple list of links cross post, for any of you who might like to be filled in.
(This would be easier with a computer, where copying the index from my blog would paste this list as clickable links for each entry, but as I have only my phone avaiable here, I prestent instead is the summary list of what you will get as links (that haven’t already been cross-posted here) if you click through to April”s index: and May’s index
Many, though not all, of those entries, include photos of projects done for Double Wars.

Eventually, my stomach insisted I get up and head over to the main house for breakfast and morning conversation, with pauses now and then to help Billy move the scaffolding to get to the next bit of fasad remdering he is removing.
Once it is all gone he will sandblast the stone clean, and fill in gaps between the stones with mortar and, where needed, small stones.
Adventures
After breakfast,  Keldor, Tania and I went out for adventures, driving over to the Kells Priory (not the one from the book of Kells, that one is closer to Dublin, this one is in Kells, Co. Kilkenny)
Kells Priory photos





The Mill
From the Priory we took the loop walk along the river past one of the old mills, and over to the other, which now houses a restaurant upstairs and a milner downstairs. We stopped at the restaurant as they wanted coffee.

I had asked earlier if Ireland has a scones and cream tradition like England does, and got a “not really”, but this restaurant had scones in addition to various chocolate deserts, and as they chose chocolate deserts, I tried the scones. Do not recommend. While they were both happy with the chocolate deserts, which looked moist and decadent, the scones were over baked  dry, too sweet, and the “cream” Came from a can and was sweetened. I managed to eat what I was given, as it wasn’t bad, but neither did it in any way compare with what I had been thinking of when I asked about scones and cream.
The bridge
Just downstream from the mill is an unusual stone bridge.

On the upstream side the suupports are spaced twice as far apart as on the downstream side.

The view back to the mill from the bridge:

And downstream:


The Pub
From the bridge we followed the loop road to the village, where we stopped at the Moat and Baily pub, where Keldor enjoyed a beer and we all enjoyed the fireplace.

the church
From there it was a short walk back to where we had parked, and a quick look at the church ruins on the other sidebof the parking from the Proriy ruins.


An early evening
When we got home it was nearly time for Mike to have a video appointment  so we relaxed and chatted in the guest cottage, to keep distractions to a minimum. But there was some sort of problem getting connected  so I am not certain it was needed, and we got word that it was clear to go to the main house around the time I started yoga.
After yoga I followed them into the house, where they were eating cheese and crackers, but then realised I was tired, so evrn though it was just over 20:00, I went back to the guest cottage with a hot water bottle and went to sleep.
